Fresh violence has again hit Plateau State, with five persons killed in coordinated attacks on communities in Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi Local Government Areas between Sunday night and the early hours of Monday. One of the attacks occurred at about 9 pm on Sunday in the Zwagal community, Jipal District of Mangu LGA, where suspected terrorists killed three people. Several others were reported missing after the raid. PUNCH Metro learnt on Monday that two more persons were killed in separate attacks in Riyom and Barkin Ladi LGAs within hours. A resident of Zwagal, Silas Nanfwang, disclosed the attack and appealed to security agencies to track down the killers. “It is a very sad incident. Security operatives should intensify efforts and go after those responsible for this attack to ensure they are brought to justice,” Nanfwang said. The Berom Youth Moulders-Association, in a statement issued on Monday by its National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, gave details of the attacks in Riyom and Barkin Ladi. According to the association, armed attackers invaded Sho village in Barkin Ladi LGA at about 5:20 pm on Sunday and killed 79-year-old Da Ishaku Pam Vwos. Earlier, at about 1:57am on Sunday, the attackers invaded the Sambak community in Hoss District, Riyom LGA, killing 42-year-old Dauda John Davou. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. However, the attackers encountered resistance as alert local vigilantes responded to the threats,” the statement said. The BYM said the weekend attacks followed earlier violence on Wednesday, when Joshua Doro Dafwel was shot in Jol and was currently receiving medical attention. On the same day, Ina Arin was killed when he and his friend, Abok Gyang, were ambushed on their way home to Dorong village in Foron District. Gyang narrowly escaped. While commending local vigilantes for responding to the attacks, the association warned that communities should not be left to defend themselves. “Communities should not be left to defend themselves against armed attacks without adequate and sustained support from security personnel,” the BYM said. The association called on President Bola Tinubu, Governor Caleb Mutfwang and relevant security agencies to urgently strengthen security deployments in vulnerable communities, investigate the killings and bring the perpetrators to justice. “We are particularly concerned that these attacks continue despite repeated security assurances and high-profile political engagements in Plateau State. “The killing of a 79-year-old man in his community further underscores the vulnerability of innocent residents, including the elderly, who deserve protection and the right to live without fear. The people of Plateau deserve more than promises; they deserve concrete action and the assurance that their lives and communities are protected. “Behind every casualty is a grieving family and a traumatised community. Our people deserve to sleep peacefully, return home safely and go about their daily activities without the constant fear of being attacked or killed,” the statement noted. The spokesperson for the Plateau State Police Command, Alabo Alfred, had yet to respond to inquiries from our correspondent about the incident as of the time of filing this report. Meanwhile, the Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council of Plateau State has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Doemak District following heightened tension after suspected gunmen burnt down seven houses in the Bong community. The curfew, which runs from 6pm to 6am daily, was imposed on Monday evening amid reports that residents were fleeing their homes, shops had closed and commercial activities had been disrupted over fears of further attacks. The Director of Press and Publicity to the Executive Chairman of the council, Danaan Sylvanus, announced the restriction in a public notice issued on Monday. He said, “In view of the security tension, Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council has imposed a curfew in Doemak. “The curfew shall be observed from 6pm to 6am. By this notice, any person found moving during this period will be treated as a security threat by the security agencies.” The council urged residents to comply strictly with the directive and cooperate with security agencies to maintain peace in the area. James Abraham
